text:
sam.k: Heads up — seeing a cluster of flaky GPUs in cluster-gpu-sfo-2. Multiple nodes reporting ECC single-bit then Xid spikes. Need to start RMA + depot-swap discussion.
anya.v: Which nodes/serials? vendor needs serials + failure logs to accept depot swap.
luis.m: Posting quick list:
- node-gpu-12 (serial: SN-A1B2C3D4, model: RTX4090-TI)
- node-gpu-13 (serial: SN-A1B2C3D5, model: RTX4090-TI)
- node-gpu-17 (serial: SN-A1B2C3F0, model: RTX4090-TI)
logs show repeating `Xid 31` + `ECC single-bit` entries around 2025-09-14T03:12Z.
ops-oncall: Please cordon/drain those nodes before we remove hardware. Window now?
sam.k: I'm starting drain now — `kubectl cordon node-gpu-12 && kubectl drain node-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then will shift traffic. ETA 12m.
vendor-bot: Ticket created: VND-234567. Status: awaiting diagnostic upload. ETA response: 72h.
margot: If vendor ETA is 72h we should consider sourcing from spare pool to keep capacity. Which depot is nearest for swap? SJC or LAX? Shipping cost diff? :thinking_face:
luis.m: Nearest depot per vendor map is SJC (1 business day depot-swap ground). LAX is same-day courier but 3x cost. We have spare cards in DFW stock (two units) but cross-country overnight ~ $220 each.
procurement: For expedited shipping we'll need approval and cost center. What's the projected downtime cost per GPU-hour? We should compare vendor-swap free vs spare-shipment charge.
anya.v: Quick back-of-envelope: peak job uses ~0.75 GPU per pod, avg revenue risk ~ $12/GPU-hour when saturated. If swap takes 72h and we lose 3 GPUs, cost ~ 72 * 3 * 12 = $2592. Overnight shipping $440 vs vendor expedite $0 (but vendor SLA uncertain). Recommend overnight spares.
sam.k: I'm +1 for overnight spares from DFW to SFO if procurement signs off. Can ops coordinate cross-dock pickup?
ops-oncall: Yep. I'll raise a logistics ticket and flag the courier. Need PO number.
procurement: PO request submitted under CC-3719. Approving expedited fee $450 per card.
vendor-bot: Diagnostic upload link: https://vendor.example.com/rma/VND-234567/upload — please attach kernel logs + `nvidia-smi -q` output.
luis.m: Uploaded `dmesg` + `nvidia-smi -q` to the vendor link (files: dmesg-node12.txt, nvidia-node12.txt). Also included recent telemetry slices.
sam.k: Confirmed drain finished on node-gpu-12/13/17. Jobs rescheduled. :white_check_mark:
margot: Logistics plan: ship spares DFW -> SFO overnight, then depot will collect faulty cards for return-to-vendor. We'll do cross-dock to avoid on-site handling.
anya.v: After we receive spares, schedule swap with on-call windowslot 02:00-04:00 local. Keep swap steps in runbook: power off, swap, boot, run `nvidia-smi -L` + quick perf smoke.
procurement: Vendor RMA notes — if vendor accepts VND-234567, they will bill return freight. We'll log costs to CC-3719 and reconcile after RMA close.
sam.k: I'll update inventory sheet with outbound spare serials and inbound RMA ticket: https://docs.internal/redwood/inventory/rma-log (added row).
ops-oncall: Post-swap, monitor for 24h for Xid/ECC regressions. If errors return, escalate to vendor priority support.
luis.m: FYI: flagged similar pattern on cluster-gpu-chi-1 two months ago — vendor replaced batch, no recurrence. Hoping same.
sam.k: Thanks all. Will update thread when spares are en route and when vendor confirms receipt of diagnostics. :shipit:
